claims.statement: Learned Motion Matching is a separate experiment that is not wired into the MoSynthStage pipeline at all: no file anywhere in the repository references its MM namespace, and it shares no type with the live architecture — no stage, no pose buffer, no skeleton, no pose set — driving Transform local position and rotation directly instead.
MM.MotionMatching is a different type in a different assembly from the MotionMatching namespace the rest of this area documents: the folder has no asmdef, so it compiles into Assembly-CSharp.
It is the repository's only Unity.Barracuda consumer, and it references UnityEditor from runtime code reached at Awake, so it could not be included in a player build as it stands.

The approach replaces the database and its brute-force search with three small neural networks — a projector standing in for nearest-neighbour lookup, an autoregressive stepper, and a decompressor reconstructing the pose — over a fifty-six float latent that is twenty-four query features concatenated with thirty-two latent floats.

The three networks can be disabled independently, which turns the debug branches into ablation switches: with the projector off the input comes from stored data rather than the user, so the chain can be run decompressor-only, decompressor plus stepper, or complete.

The class carries no Serializable attribute while the driver holds it as a plain public field, so it would not be serialized and would be null when the driver calls into it at Awake — as committed the entry point appears non-functional.
It uses the legacy Input.GetAxisRaw rather than the Input System asset the rest of the project uses, and hardcodes a sixty hertz step in three separate places rather than reading the frame time.
